**`pm:queue` → `needs-user-decision`.** PM round 6, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`. Not dispatched — and I am correcting a label I set myself.

## First, my own error in the transfer

This card's body says, verbatim: *"Filed unassigned, no `pm:queue` — for triage to grade."* When I rebuilt it here from `objectstack-ai/objectstack#7345` earlier today I attached `pm:queue` anyway. That is a half-state of my own making: the body says one thing, the label says another, and there is no triage grading comment on it (comment count: zero). Corrected now.

## Why it is not dispatchable, beyond the missing grading

Four dispositions, **no option recommended**, and option 1 ("leave it") is explicitly defensible in the card's own words. That alone makes it a decision. But there is a sharper reason I want on the record before anyone picks this up, because disposition 3 reads like free polish and **is not**.

**Disposition 3 — "distinguish *not visible to you* from *does not exist* on the record page" — partially undoes a deliberate server-side choice.**

The card's own evidence shows the server answering:

```
GET /api/v1/data/showcase_invoice/9oAya50sd_E-PEWH
404 {"error":"Record … not found in showcase_invoice","code":"RECORD_NOT_FOUND"}
```

**404, not 403** — and that is not an accident of implementation. The record is filtered out of the row set *before* the by-id read, so from the server's perspective it does not exist for this principal. Returning 404 rather than 403 is the standard way to avoid confirming that a record exists to someone not permitted to see it.

So changing the UI to say *"you do not have access to this record"* would tell the viewer **the record exists** — which the server deliberately declined to tell them. That is an information-disclosure decision, not a copy fix. It may well be the right call here (an approver already knows the record exists — they were routed a request about it, and the drawer shows them its payload snapshot), but *that* argument is exactly the kind that has to be made explicitly rather than assumed by a dev polishing a message.

The card notes `sys_inbox_message` renders the honest message for the same persona. Worth knowing — but it is evidence that the two surfaces disagree, not evidence about which one is right.

This lands squarely on the maintainer floor: **安全/权限边界** — a "fix" to access-control messaging is a disguised product decision.

## Where each disposition lands

- **1 (leave it)** — no work; defensible per the card.
- **2 (suppress the link when the viewer cannot read the target)** — needs a per-row readability probe the inbox does not do today. Cost is real; no disclosure question. This is the disposition that is purely UX.
- **3 (fix the landing message)** — **the disclosure question above.** Cheapest to implement, not cheapest to decide.
- **4 (implicit read for approvers)** — the card already flags it as a security-model change, and the transfer note is binding: if it is ever taken it goes back to `objectstack-ai/objectstack` as a contract-first split, ⛔ **not** done here.

**No PM recommendation.** I could argue 2, or 1, or 3-with-the-approver-exception, and the choice turns on how much existence-disclosure an approver is entitled to — which is yours, not mine.

## Not a blocked approval, for calibration

The drawer carries the request's payload snapshot (record title, object, subtotal, account, status) and the decision itself works — the verification run approved this exact request from the drawer. What is broken is an **affordance**: the inbox offers a link that, for the person it is offered to, lands on a page saying the record may have been deleted. Real, worth fixing, not urgent.

## Zone 1 — RULED, both branches pre-ruled. Do not escalate.

Maintainer, 2026-08-19, verbatim 「全部接受」, recorded on this card:

> ## Ruling: Option 2, with Option 1 as the pre-ruled fallback
> - **Option 2**: an Approvals Inbox row **suppresses the record link when the viewer cannot read the target** — a readability probe (batchable) decides per row. The server's deliberate 404-not-403 semantics stay completely untouched; the dead-end affordance disappears.
> - **Pre-ruled fallback**: if the probe's cost measures too high in practice (**the dev reports the measurement rather than deciding silently**), fall back to Option 1 — leave the link behaviour as-is and state in the approval drawer that decisions are made from the payload snapshot.
> - **Rejected**: Option 3 … Option 4 …

## ⛔ The two rejected options, and why option 3 is the dangerous one

**Option 3 — changing the landing message to "you do not have access to this record" — is rejected, and it is the one you will be tempted by** because it is a one-line copy change. It is not copy polish. The server answers:

```
GET /api/v1/data/showcase_invoice/9oAya50sd_E-PEWH
404 {"error":"Record … not found in showcase_invoice","code":"RECORD_NOT_FOUND"}
```

**404, not 403 — deliberately.** The record is filtered out of the row set *before* the by-id read, so from the server's perspective it does not exist for this principal. Saying "you do not have access" would tell the viewer **the record exists**, which the server declined to tell them. That is an information-disclosure decision, and it has been made: **no.**

**Option 4 (an implicit read grant for approvers) is rejected too**, and if it ever comes back it goes to `objectstack-ai/objectstack` as a contract-first split — ⛔ never here.

## Zone 2 — the cost measurement is a deliverable, and it selects the branch

The ruling hands you the fallback so you do not have to come back and ask. **Measure the probe, then pick:**

- **Cheap** (batchable in one call alongside what the inbox already fetches, no per-row round trip) ⇒ ship **Option 2**.
- **Too expensive** (a request per row, or a call the inbox does not otherwise make) ⇒ ship **Option 1**: leave the link alone and state in the approval drawer that decisions are made from the payload snapshot.

**Report the measurement either way** — what the probe costs, how many calls, on what render. ⛔ Do not silently choose the cheaper code path; the ruling asks for the number, and "I judged it too costly" without one is not a report.

## What is NOT broken — calibration, so you don't over-fix

The approval itself **works**. The drawer carries the request's payload snapshot (record title, object, subtotal, account, status) and a previous verification run approved this exact request from the drawer. What is broken is an **affordance**: the inbox offers a link that, for the person it is offered to, lands on a page saying the record may have been deleted. Real, worth fixing, **not urgent** — so ⛔ do not grow this into a rework of the inbox.

Note also that `sys_inbox_message` renders the honest message for the same persona. That is evidence the two surfaces **disagree** — it is not evidence about which one is right, and ⛔ it is not licence to make this surface match it (that would be option 3).

## Tests

- Viewer **cannot** read the target ⇒ **no link rendered** (Option 2) — this is the change; it must fail before your edit.
- Viewer **can** read the target ⇒ link renders and works, unchanged.
- The approval decision path is untouched in both cases — **pin it**, because it is the thing that currently works and must keep working.
- ⛔ No test asserts anything about the server's 404 vs 403. That semantics is out of scope in both directions.

If you ship Option 1 instead: pin the drawer's new wording and say plainly in the report that the link behaviour is unchanged by design.

Reverse-verify: restore the row change, keep the tests, **predict which go red before running**, report predicted vs observed. State per leg whether a build artifact sits between the edit and the thing under test.

## Gates

Derive from your diff (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is **objectstack-only**). Run vitest **from the repo root** — the reason is not that package-scoped runs are refused (17 packages own a standalone `vitest.config.ts` and are not refused) but that a package-scoped run uses **a different config than CI does**. If your change adds user-visible copy, expect `check:i18n-keys` / `check:i18n-drift` and all ten locale packs. Changeset per `check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s verdict; `patch` or `minor`, ⛔ **never `major`**.

⛔ Do not background a long check and end your turn. ⛔ No exhaustive paginated API sweeps.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first body line `Fixes #5211`. **State which branch you shipped and the measurement that chose it, in the first paragraph of the PR body.** Push the branch early. Return the JSON report and post it as a comment whose first line is the literal `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker.
